sections.heading: Contract basics and classifications
sections.intro: A contract is an enforceable agreement between competent parties to do, or not do, something lawful in exchange for consideration. Expect to attach several labels to one contract.
points: A typical purchase contract is **express, bilateral, and executory** until closing; an option is **express and unilateral**; an installment land contract stays executory for years.
In everyday speech “executed” means signed, but in classification it means **fully performed**. A contract signed today that closes next month is executory.

**Contracts affecting brokers** include the broker–salesperson independent contractor agreement, listing and buyer agency agreements, contracts of sale, and leases. The independent contractor agreement must be written.

head: Label
Meaning
Example
rows: Terms stated in words, oral or written
Owner accepts work knowing payment is expected
Contract of sale; exclusive right to sell listing
Promise for an act; one side bound
Option; open listing; bonus to the first agent who brings a buyer
Valid until the protected party cancels
Exists, but a court won't enforce it
Oral land sale; suit after 6 years

sections.heading: Essential elements of a valid contract
sections.intro: The syllabus lists five essentials: competent parties, mutual agreement, lawful objective, consideration, and a writing. Which one is missing decides the label.
points: **Competent parties**: in New York a minor (infant) is anyone under 18.
Only the minor may disaffirm (cancel), before or within a reasonable time after turning 18. Continuing to pay long after 18 **ratifies** (confirms) the contract.
**Mutual agreement** (a meeting of the minds) is an offer plus an acceptance of exactly its terms, freely given.
**Consideration** is a bargained-for exchange of value: money, property, a promise, or **forbearance** (holding off on a legal right, as when a lender delays foreclosure).
Exchanged promises are enough, so a deposit is customary but not required. Courts don't weigh adequacy: a sale at half price still has consideration.
**Past consideration** (work already done for free) does not support a promise, unless the promise is in a signed writing that states it (GOL §5-1105).
**Writing**: land sale contracts and leases over one year (GOL §5-703). **Recording is not an element**; it only gives the public constructive notice.
**Power of attorney**: an agent (attorney-in-fact) signing a real estate contract needs written authority, which ends at the principal's death.

head: Situation
Status
Who can get out
rows: A party who did not sign

sections.heading: Offer, acceptance, and genuine consent
sections.intro: The **offeror** makes the offer; the **offeree** accepts or rejects it. Each counteroffer swaps the roles.
points: Listing prices and ads are **invitations to negotiate**; a buyer's “I accept your price” email is itself an offer.
Acceptance must match the offer exactly. Any change, even a new closing date, is a **counteroffer** that rejects and kills the original offer.
A later “I accept” of the dead offer is only a new offer. A mere question (“Is the price firm?”) is not a rejection.
**Silence** is not acceptance.
An offer may be **revoked any time before acceptance**, unless it was made irrevocable. The classic way is an **option** the buyer paid for.
Mailbox rule: an acceptance is effective **when sent**; a revocation only **when received**. The offeror may require actual receipt instead.
Offers also end by lapse of time, rejection, **death or incapacity** of either party, or destruction of the property; a signed contract survives death.

A **caveat** is a warning. **Caveat emptor** (buyer beware) limits a New York seller's duty to volunteer defects. But concealment is fraud, statutory disclosures apply, and licensees must disclose known material defects.

head: Problem
What it looks like
Effect
rows: Lie or concealment about a material fact
Voidable; rescind or sue for damages
Abuse of trust (caregiver and elderly owner)
Both wrong about a basic fact (house already burned)
Clear refusal before the due date

example.title: Worked example: mailbox timeline
steps: Facts: the seller mails a revocation on the 3rd; the buyer mails an acceptance on the 4th; the revocation arrives on the 5th and the acceptance on the 6th.
Step 1: The acceptance took effect when sent, on the 4th.
Step 2: The revocation could only take effect on receipt, the 5th, too late.
Answer: A contract formed on the 4th, unless the offer required actual receipt of the acceptance.

sections.heading: Statute of frauds, parol evidence, and deadlines to sue
sections.intro: New York's **statute of frauds** for land is in the General Obligations Law (GOL §5-703).
points: A contract to sell real property, or to lease it for **more than one year**, needs a writing that states the consideration.
The writing must be **signed by the party to be charged** (the one being sued) or by an agent authorized in writing.

The statute says “void,” but courts treat an oral deal as **unenforceable**: it can still be performed voluntarily. If only the seller signed, the buyer can enforce it against the seller, not the reverse.
A listing broker is a **special agent** (authorized only for a specific task) and normally cannot sign a sale contract for the seller.
Leases of one year or less may be oral, even one that starts in the future. The one-year limit measures the lease term, not the time from the agreement (Young v. Dake).
Options and rights of first refusal need writings, and emails or e-signatures can qualify.
**Part performance** can support specific performance: possession, payment, and improvements explainable only by the oral deal (GOL §5-703(4)).
A promise to pay a fee for negotiating a real estate sale, lease, or loan must be in a signed writing. This covers even a finder who only makes the introduction (GOL §5-701(a)(10)).

That rule **does not apply** to auctioneers, attorneys, or **duly licensed real estate brokers and salespersons**. So a licensed broker's oral commission agreement can be enforced. Put listings in writing anyway.

**Parol evidence rule** (parol means oral): earlier oral side deals cannot contradict a complete signed writing. A **merger (entire agreement) clause** confirms the writing is the whole deal. Fraud, duress, and mistake can still be proved.
Statute of limitations: **6 years** from the breach for contract suits (CPLR §213(2)).
**Laches** bars equitable relief after an unreasonable, prejudicial delay.
The Uniform Commercial Code covers goods and checks, not land.

example.title: Worked example: statute of limitations
steps: Facts: a seller breached on March 15, 2024.
Step 1: Add the 6-year contract period (CPLR §213(2)): 2024 + 6 = 2030.
Answer: The buyer must sue by March 15, 2030; 10 years is the adverse possession period, not the contract period.

sections.heading: Breach and remedies
sections.intro: A **breach** is a failure to perform without legal excuse. The injured party picks a remedy, unless the contract pre-sets one.
points: **Specific performance** (a court order to complete the deal) exists because each parcel is unique. A buyer who sues for it can file a **notice of pendency** (lis pendens) to warn later buyers.
**Liquidated damages** (a sum agreed in advance, usually the down payment) must be a reasonable estimate, not a **penalty**.
In New York a seller may generally keep a down payment up to **10%** when the buyer defaults without legal excuse, even after reselling at a profit (Maxton Builders v. Lo Galbo, 1986).
**Earnest money** (a good-faith deposit) is not refunded just because the buyer changes her mind, and it does not automatically become the broker's commission; the contract decides who gets it.
Contracts end by performance, mutual release, **novation** (replacing the contract or a party), impossibility, or operation of law (statute of limitations, bankruptcy).

head: Remedy
What it does
Typical use
rows: Buyer wants the property, not money
Buyer defaults; seller keeps the deposit
Rewrites the document to match the deal

example.title: Worked example: compensatory vs. liquidated damages
steps: Facts: a buyer breaches a $500,000 contract with no liquidated damages clause. The seller resells for $470,000 and pays $4,000 in extra carrying costs.
Step 2: Compare a $425,000 contract whose 10% down payment is liquidated damages: $425,000 × 10% = $42,500.
Answer: $34,000; in the second case the seller generally keeps all $42,500, even if she later resells for more.

sections.heading: Listing agreements and 19 NYCRR §175.24
sections.intro: A **listing agreement** is an employment (agency) contract hiring a broker to find a buyer or tenant. It is not a contract to sell, and the broker is a special agent.
points: Exclusive residential listings must include the DOS explanation, **printed on or attached**, in at least **6-point type** (§175.24).
Residential here means 1–4 family, condo, or co-op, **not** vacant land.
The explanation must be **signed or initialed** by the homeowner or her agent. Nothing is filed with DOS.
The explanation says: under exclusive right to sell, the owner pays the present broker even if she or another broker finds the buyer.
Under exclusive agency, the owner owes nothing if she finds the buyer, but owes **both the selling broker and the present broker** if another broker does.

If the broker belongs to a multiple listing service (MLS), the exclusive residential listing must let the owner choose to have negotiated offers submitted through the **listing broker or the selling broker** (§175.24(c)).
A listing can't continue automatically past its fixed end date (§175.15). A **protection (carryover) clause** covering buyers introduced during the term is allowed.
**Net listings** are illegal (§175.19); commissions are negotiable.
Give the seller the **RPL §443 agency disclosure** before she signs, and a copy of the signed listing **immediately** (§175.12).
The listing belongs to the **broker**, so it stays with the firm when the salesperson leaves.
The fee is earned when the broker produces a **ready, willing, and able** buyer on the listing terms, even if the seller backs out, unless payment depends on closing.
In an open listing only the **procuring cause** is paid: the broker whose efforts started the unbroken chain to the sale.
A listing ends by sale, expiration, mutual agreement, or automatically on the owner's **death or incapacity** or the property's destruction; an owner who revokes early may owe damages.

head: Listing
Who is paid on a sale during the term
Owner finds the buyer
Exam angle
rows: Listing broker, plus the selling broker if another broker finds the buyer
Listing broker on a lease made during the term
Rental version of exclusive right to sell
Broker keeps everything above the seller's net

example.title: Worked example: protection clause
steps: Facts: a listing with a 60-day protection clause expires June 30. On August 20 the owner, who has not relisted, sells to a buyer the broker showed in May.
Step 1: July has 31 days, so August 20 is day 31 + 20 = 51 after expiration.
Answer: Day 51 is inside the 60 days, so the broker is likely owed the commission.

sections.heading: Buyer agency agreements
sections.intro: A **buyer agency agreement** makes the broker the buyer's agent, owing her fiduciary duties, and sets the fee. The syllabus calls it the exclusive right to represent.
points: Give the buyer the **§443 disclosure** before she signs the agreement; give it to the seller or listing agent at the first substantive contact.

**Who pays does not decide who is represented**: a buyer's agent paid out of the listing broker's commission still represents the buyer. Pay from more than one party needs the **client's** consent (§175.7).

Since August 17, 2024, National Association of Realtors (NAR) policy from its settlement requires MLS participants to sign a written agreement on the broker's compensation before touring a home with a buyer. It is association policy, not a New York statute.

head: Buyer agreement
Broker is paid when
Buyer finds the home herself
rows: Buyer buys a described property during the term
Anyone but the buyer finds the property
That broker finds the property bought

sections.heading: Binders, purchase offers, and limits on licensee drafting
sections.intro: A **binder** outlines the key terms before the formal contract. It is also called a receipt, memorandum of sale, or purchase offer. In New York City the accepted-offer summary is a **deal sheet**.
points: A binder **“subject to a formal contract”** binds no one yet, so the seller may take a higher offer despite the buyer's deposit. A signed binder stating all essential terms, with no such reservation, can be enforceable.
Non-lawyers may not practice law (Judiciary Law §478). They also may not charge to prepare instruments affecting real estate (Judiciary Law §484). Both are misdemeanors.
DOS separately disciplines licensees for unauthorized practice (Duncan & Hill Realty v. Department of State, 1978).
A licensee may prepare a simple fill-in-the-blanks contract that is **subject to each party's attorney's approval** (DOS Legal Memorandum LI04, 2020).
Or she may use a form approved by a **joint bar association–Realtor committee**, filling in only facts: names, price, closing date and place, property description.
She may not devise legal terms. Adding any provision or rider (addendum) means the whole contract must be subject to attorney approval.
No legal advice, no discouraging lawyers, and no separate fee or share of attorney fees.
**Attorney approval clause**: each side's attorney may disapprove in writing within the contract's window, often three business days. It is common upstate, where non-lawyers fill in the form.
If no disapproval arrives in time, the contingency is **deemed waived** and the contract binds.
The attorney may disapprove for **any reason or no reason**, even the client's change of heart, as long as it is timely (Moran v. Erk, N.Y. 2008).

example.title: Worked example: attorney-review deadline
steps: Facts: three business days, excluding weekends and holidays, from full execution on a Friday.
Step 1: Start the day after signing and skip the weekend: Monday (1), Tuesday (2), Wednesday (3).
Answer: Wednesday. Counting Friday itself or the weekend gives the wrong day.

sections.heading: What goes into a New York contract of sale
sections.intro: The contract of sale is the road map to closing. Standard forms differ for houses, condos, co-ops, commercial property, installment sales, and options.
points: The **merger (entire agreement) clause** shuts out earlier side deals. Separately, at closing the contract **merges into the deed**, so nothing survives unless the contract says it survives.

**Limit (liquidation) of seller's liability**: many forms say that if the seller cannot convey the promised title, her only liability is to return the down payment and pay the buyer's title search and survey costs.
**Broker clause**: names the brokers who brought about the sale; downstate contracts usually omit the commission amount.

head: Clause
What it does
Watch for
rows: Check the address against the deed, tax map, and survey
Buyer accepts listed covenants, easements, zoning
If not violated and use isn't blocked
Names the deed to be delivered
“On or about” isn't time of the essence
Seller holds sale proceeds in trust for recent improvements (Lien Law §13(5))
Seller bears the risk until title or possession passes

sections.heading: Preparing and signing the contract in New York
sections.intro: **Downstate** (New York City, Long Island, Westchester, and nearby counties) the seller's attorney drafts the contract. In much of **upstate**, a licensee fills in an approved form subject to attorney approval.
points: Downstate: deal sheet to the attorneys; the **seller's attorney drafts**; the buyer's attorney reviews.
The **buyer signs first** and pays the down payment. The seller signs and delivers last, and only then is it binding. The buyer goes first because her signed contract and check are the offer.

Before signing, confirm the terms with the seller: every owner's name, price, inclusions and exclusions, closing and move-out dates, and acceptable contingencies. Signing may be in person, by mail, or electronic.
Gather the prior deed, prior title policy, survey, **certificate of occupancy**, personal data (names, marital status, Social Security numbers), and tax bills.
Check the certificate of occupancy: does the legal use match, say, a two-family? Were additions permitted?
**Property description**: a house is usually identified by street address and tax map number, often with the deed's legal description attached.
For vacant land, attach or refer to the deed, filed map, or survey. Verify everything against the prior deed and survey.
The deed itself needs a formal **legal description**: metes and bounds or a lot on a filed map.
Down payment downstate: usually **10%**, paid to the **seller's attorney as escrowee** (the neutral holder of the deposit).
Upstate: a negotiated, often smaller deposit, frequently held by the listing broker. Paying the seller directly leaves the buyer unprotected.
Broker escrow rules (§175.1): deposit into a separate, federally insured account within **3 business days**, keeping it secure until then.
No **commingling** (mixing) or **conversion** (using). Salespersons hand deposits to the broker promptly.
Attorney-held money has an extra safeguard: the **Lawyers' Fund for Client Protection** can repay losses caused by a dishonest New York lawyer.
Before the buyer is bound, deliver each disclosure that applies. First, the §443 agency disclosure, acknowledged.
Next, the seller's **Property Condition Disclosure Statement (PCDS)**. The $500 credit opt-out ended in 2024.
For **pre-1978** housing: the lead pamphlet, disclosure, warning statement, and a **10-day** inspection opportunity.
Where it applies, the agricultural district notice (RPL §333-c).

example.title: Worked example: down payment and cash to close
steps: Facts: $720,000 price, 10% down at signing, a $5,000 binder credited, and an 80% loan.
Step 2: Due at signing = $72,000 − $5,000 credit = $67,000.
Step 4: Cash at closing = $720,000 − $72,000 − $576,000 = $72,000, before costs.
Answer: $67,000 at signing and $72,000 at closing, before costs.

sections.heading: Contingencies
sections.intro: A **contingency** makes performance depend on an event. It protects only a party who meets its deadline and notice terms.
points: **Mortgage contingency**: a buyer who applies promptly in good faith, is denied or offered less than the contract amount, and gives timely notice may cancel and recover her deposit.

A buyer who never applies cannot use it, and a clause deeming it **waived** without timely notice is enforced. The party it benefits may **waive** it (for example, by paying cash), and the seller stays bound.
Financing types: conventional, **FHA or VA**, **purchase money mortgage** (seller financing), and assumption.
FHA and VA loans carry an amendatory clause: the buyer may cancel without losing her deposit if the appraisal is low.
An **assumption** needs lender approval, and the seller stays liable unless released.

**Kick-out clause**: with a sale-of-home contingency, the seller keeps marketing and, on a backup offer, gives the first buyer a set time (for example, 72 hours) to drop the contingency or lose the deal.

head: Contingency
Key rule
rows: Good-faith application; meet the deadline and notice terms
Timely disapproval, any reason; silence binds
Notice within the window or it lapses
Rejection usually ends the deal; deposit returned

example.title: Worked example: loan commitment shortfall
steps: Facts: the contract requires a $480,000 commitment; the lender commits $430,000.
Answer: The contingency is unmet, so the buyer may cancel with timely notice rather than find $50,000.

sections.heading: Options, rights of first refusal, and installment land contracts
sections.intro: Each gives a future right to buy or a way to pay over time. Know who is bound and when title passes.
points: An option lets the **optionee** buy at a fixed price within a set time.
The paid **optionor** is bound and cannot revoke, even by refunding the fee.
Exercising the option creates a bilateral sale contract, and the fee is often credited. If it lapses, the optionor keeps the fee.
Options must be written and may be recorded (RPL §294). A **lease with option to buy** adds rent credits, and breaching the lease can cost the option.

**Right of first refusal (ROFR)**: no preset price and no power to force a sale. When the owner decides to accept a bona fide offer, the holder may match it; materially better terms offered later must be re-offered. Condo boards often hold one.
Installment land contract: the **vendee** (buyer) gets possession and **equitable title** (the right to legal title once paid).
The **vendor** (seller) keeps **legal title** and delivers the deed when paid.
The buyer gains cash flow (little down, no bank loan); the seller spreads the taxable gain and keeps title as security.
An existing mortgage's due-on-sale clause may require lender **forbearance**.
New York may make a vendor **foreclose** rather than forfeit a vendee who paid a substantial part (Bean v. Walker, 1983).
Vendees should **record** the contract or a memorandum (RPL §294).

example.title: Worked example: lease-option balance
steps: Facts: $400,000 price, $10,000 option fee credited, $250 rent credit for each of 18 months.
Step 1: $250 × 18 = $4,500 in rent credits.
Answer: $385,500 still owed.

sections.heading: Risk of loss and time of the essence
sections.intro: Between signing and closing, two questions arise: who bears a casualty loss, and how firm is the closing date?
points: The **Uniform Vendor and Purchaser Risk Act** replaces the common-law **equitable conversion** rule, which put the risk on the buyer from signing (GOL §5-1311).
It applies **unless the contract expressly says otherwise**. A taking by eminent domain counts like destruction.
Early possession shifts the risk to the buyer, so she should insure.

Leases: a tenant whose unit becomes untenantable by fire or the elements through no fault of her own may **quit and surrender** and owe no further rent, unless a written agreement says otherwise (RPL §227).
A closing set “on or about” a date (the **law date**) is a target. Without time of the essence, either side gets a **reasonable adjournment**.
With a **time of the essence** clause, a party not ready that day is in **material breach**.
Time can be made of the essence later by **clear, unequivocal notice** setting a **reasonable** date and warning that missing it is a default.
The party declaring a default must itself be **ready, willing, and able**; a seller with an unpaid judgment lien cannot hold the buyer in default.

head: Before closing
Loss
Result
rows: Buyer may cancel and recover her deposit
Sale proceeds with a price abatement
Any part, not the seller's fault

example.title: Worked example: price abatement
steps: Facts: before title or possession passes, an $8,000 shed is destroyed on a $500,000 contract.
Step 1: The shed is an immaterial part, so neither side can cancel.
Answer: The price is abated (reduced) to $500,000 − $8,000 = $492,000.

sections.heading: Assignment, novation, death of a party, and leases
sections.intro: Contracts can change hands. The exam asks whether the original party is still liable.
points: **Assignment** transfers rights; **delegation** transfers duties.
A contract silent on assignment is generally assignable, for example to the buyer's LLC. But an **anti-assignment clause** is enforced, and personal-service contracts need consent.
The **assignor** (the party who transferred) stays liable; consenting to an assignment is not a release.
**Novation** substitutes a new contract or party and **releases** the old one, as a lender's release does on a mortgage assumption.
Death ends an offer and a listing, but a signed **contract of sale binds the estate**.
A sale doesn't end a lease: the buyer takes **subject to existing leases**. A lease assignment transfers the whole remaining term, a sublease only part, and neither releases the tenant.
An automatic lease renewal binds the tenant only if the landlord sends a written reminder **15 to 30 days** before her notice deadline (GOL §5-905).

head: Transfer
Original party released?
rows: No, unless the landlord releases the tenant

guides.title: Real Estate Finance
guides.overview: Covers the note and mortgage, lien priority, New York foreclosure and deficiency rules, lenders and the secondary market, loan types, mortgage insurance, adjustable-rate mortgages (ARMs), points and APR, lending laws, underwriting, and predatory lending. The exam's favorite ideas: the **mortgagor** is the borrower, **points** are figured on the loan amount, and New York foreclosure goes through **court**.

numbers.label: Of the loan amount, never the purchase price
Conventional loans above this (less than 20% down) usually require PMI
PMI: borrower may request cancellation when the balance reaches this share of original value
Scheduled share of original value at which PMI ends automatically (midpoint at latest)
FHA minimum down payment with a 580+ credit score (10% for scores of 500–579)
Annual FHA MIP under 10% down; 11 years at 10%+ (since June 3, 2013)
VA loan with full entitlement when the price does not exceed the appraised value
Minimum age for an FHA reverse mortgage (HECM)
Traditional conventional ratios: housing (front-end) / total debt (back-end)
Loan Estimate after application; Closing Disclosure before consummation; TILA rescission period
Pre-foreclosure notice before a NY home-loan foreclosure filing (RPAPL §1304)
Settlement conference, counted from the filing of proof of service (CPLR 3408)
Life of a notice of pendency (lis pendens) unless extended
Deadline to seek a deficiency judgment after delivery of the referee's deed (RPAPL §1371)
Lender must present the satisfaction of mortgage for recording after payoff (RPL §275)
ECOA: notice of action taken on a completed credit application
NY late-charge cap on owner-occupied 1–6 family and co-op loans (FHA and VA excepted)
NY civil usury ceiling / criminal usury threshold

mustKnow: The **promissory note** (bond) is the personal promise to repay; the **mortgage** is the security instrument that creates the lien.
**Mortgagor** = the borrower, who gives the mortgage; **mortgagee** = the lender, who receives it.
New York is a **lien-theory** state: the borrower keeps title and possession until a foreclosure sale.
Mortgagor duties: pay the debt, pay **taxes and assessments**, keep the property **insured**, and keep it in repair.
**Acceleration** = whole balance due on default; **escalation** = the rate goes up.
**Alienation (due-on-sale)** = the loan is callable on transfer.
**Defeasance** ends the lien at payoff; a New York lender must present the satisfaction for recording within **30 days**.
Recording order sets priority under New York's **race-notice** act, but **real property tax liens** come first regardless of date.
A foreclosure cuts off properly joined **junior** liens but never affects a **senior** lien.
**Subject to**: the buyer is not personally liable.
**Assumption**: the buyer is primarily liable and the seller secondarily liable, unless there is a novation or release.
New York mortgage foreclosure is **judicial**: 90-day notice, lawsuit and lis pendens, settlement conference, judgment of foreclosure and sale, then auction by a **referee**.
A co-op share loan is the exception to judicial foreclosure: the lender uses a nonjudicial UCC sale.
The **equity of redemption** lasts until the sale; New York has **no statutory redemption** after it.
NY deficiency = debt minus the **higher** of the sale price or fair market value; the motion is due within **90 days** of delivery of the referee's deed.
The **primary market** originates loans; the **secondary market** (Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac) buys them so lenders can lend again.
**Ginnie Mae** (inside HUD) guarantees securities backed by FHA, VA, and USDA loans; it does not buy loans.
A **mortgage broker** arranges loans with other lenders' money; a **mortgage banker** funds and closes loans in its own name.
**Conventional** = no government insurance or guarantee.
**Conforming** = meets Fannie/Freddie rules; **jumbo** = above the conforming loan limit.
**FHA insures** (borrower pays MIP) and **VA guarantees** (borrower pays a funding fee); private lenders make the loans, and neither program uses PMI.
PMI protects the lender: request cancellation at **80%** of original value, automatic at **78%**; original value = the lower of price or appraisal.
**SONYMA** (State of New York Mortgage Agency) uses tax-exempt bond money for below-market loans, mainly to first-time buyers.
ARM rate = **index + margin**, then apply the periodic and lifetime **caps**; the margin never changes.
A **payment cap** can cause **negative amortization** when the payment does not cover the interest due.
**APR** = interest plus prepaid finance charges (points, origination and broker fees, mortgage insurance); it excludes appraisal, title, credit report, taxes, and escrows.
TRID: **Loan Estimate** within 3 business days after application; **Closing Disclosure** received at least 3 business days before consummation.
TILA **rescission** (3 business days) covers refinances (only the new money if the same lender refinances) and equity loans on a principal residence, never the loan used to buy the home.
Ad **triggering terms** (down payment, number of payments or term, payment amount, finance charge) require the down payment, repayment terms, and APR.
ECOA protects **marital status**, age, and **public-assistance income** as well as race, color, religion, national origin, and sex; decision notice within 30 days.
Maximum PITI = the **lower** of income × front-end ratio or income × back-end ratio − other monthly debts.
**Subprime** is not illegal; lending is **predatory** when it uses abusive terms such as flipping, packing, hidden fees, or ignoring the ability to repay.
New York **high-cost home loans** may not include flipping, financed single-premium credit insurance, or negative amortization, and require a counseling notice (Banking Law §6-l).

traps.trap: The mortgagor is the lender, since it holds the mortgage.
traps.truth: The mortgagor is the borrower, who gives the mortgage; the lender receives it and is the mortgagee.

traps.trap: Points are figured on the purchase price.
traps.truth: Points are a percentage of the loan amount: 2 points on a $300,000 loan cost $6,000, whatever the price.

traps.trap: PMI drops off automatically at 80%.
traps.truth: PMI ends automatically at 78% (or the loan's midpoint); 80% of original value is only the borrower-request point. FHA MIP follows separate rules and often lasts for the life of the loan.

traps.trap: A New York deficiency is the debt minus the auction price.
traps.truth: The deficiency is the debt minus the higher of the sale price or the court-set fair market value. The lender must move within 90 days of the referee's deed.

traps.trap: After a subject-to or assumption sale, the buyer alone owes any deficiency.
traps.truth: Subject to: only the seller is liable, because the buyer never promised to pay. Assumption: the buyer is primarily liable; the seller stays secondarily liable unless released by the lender or a novation.

traps.trap: New York owners can redeem the home after the foreclosure auction.
traps.truth: The equity of redemption ends at the sale; New York has no post-sale statutory redemption period.

traps.trap: Add the ARM margin to the teaser rate or to last year's rate.
traps.truth: Add the margin to the current index, then apply the periodic and lifetime caps; the lowest limit controls.

traps.trap: A deed in lieu gives the lender the same clean title as a foreclosure.
traps.truth: Junior liens survive a deed in lieu, because it is a voluntary transfer. Only a foreclosure cuts off junior liens that were joined.

traps.trap: Every home loan carries a 3-day right to rescind.
traps.truth: Rescission covers non-purchase loans secured by a principal residence, such as refinances and equity loans; the purchase mortgage is exempt.

traps.trap: The Loan Estimate must arrive 3 business days before closing.
traps.truth: The Loan Estimate is due within 3 business days after the application. The 3-days-before-closing rule is for the Closing Disclosure.

traps.trap: A referral payment is legal under RESPA if it is disclosed or called a marketing fee.
traps.truth: Anything of value given for referring settlement business is a kickback, whatever the label or disclosure; only payment for services actually performed is allowed.

traps.trap: A prequalification or preapproval means the loan is approved.
traps.truth: Only the lender's written commitment approves the loan, and it still has conditions such as appraisal and title. Prequalification is unverified; preapproval is conditional.

mnemonics.name: -OR gives, -EE receives
mnemonics.meaning: Mortgagor (borrower) gives the mortgage; mortgagee (lender) receives it, like grantor/grantee and lessor/lessee.

mnemonics.name: PITI
mnemonics.meaning: Principal, Interest, Taxes, Insurance: the housing payment used in the front-end ratio.

mnemonics.name: Ginnie = Government
mnemonics.meaning: Ginnie Mae is the government-owned one (inside HUD) and guarantees securities; Fannie and Freddie are government-sponsored enterprises that buy loans.

mnemonics.name: Ask at 80, auto at 78
mnemonics.meaning: PMI: request cancellation at 80% of original value; automatic at 78%; final stop at the loan's midpoint.

mnemonics.name: Index + margin, then caps
mnemonics.meaning: ARM order: add the margin to the index, then apply the periodic and lifetime caps.

formulas.name: Cost of points
formulas.formula: Points cost = Loan amount × points %

formulas.name: Number of points
formulas.formula: Points = Points cost ÷ Loan amount

formulas.name: Loan-to-value ratio
formulas.formula: LTV = Loan ÷ lower of price or appraised value

formulas.name: One month's interest
formulas.formula: Monthly interest = Balance (or amount drawn) × annual rate ÷ 12
formulas.example: $240,000 × 6.5% ÷ 12 = $1,300; that is the whole payment on an interest-only loan, and a construction loan charges it only on funds drawn

formulas.name: ARM rate
formulas.formula: New rate = Index + Margin, no higher than old rate + periodic cap or initial rate + lifetime cap
formulas.example: 4.60% + 2.75% = 7.35%, but a 2% periodic cap from 5.25% limits it to 7.25%

formulas.name: Maximum PITI
formulas.formula: Max PITI = lower of (monthly income × front ratio) or (monthly income × back ratio − other debts)

formulas.name: Income needed
formulas.formula: Annual income = PITI ÷ ratio × 12

formulas.name: PMI cancellation balances
formulas.formula: Request = Original value × 80%; automatic = Original value × 78%
formulas.example: Original value $500,000: request at $400,000, automatic at $390,000

formulas.name: New York deficiency
formulas.formula: Deficiency = Debt with interest and costs − higher of sale price or fair market value

formulas.name: Redemption amount
formulas.formula: Redeem = Principal + accrued interest + allowed costs

formulas.name: Partial release price
formulas.formula: Release price = (Blanket loan ÷ number of lots) × release %

formulas.name: Cash to assume a loan
formulas.formula: Cash = (Price − balance assumed) + assumption fee

formulas.name: Prepayment penalty (commercial note)
formulas.formula: Penalty = Penalty rate × (amount prepaid − penalty-free allowance)

sections.heading: Note, mortgage, and New York's lien theory
sections.intro: Every home loan uses two documents with two different jobs. Exam questions love to swap them.
points: The **promissory note** (often called a bond in New York) is the borrower's personal promise to repay.
The **mortgage** is the security instrument that pledges the property and creates a voluntary, specific **lien**.
Without a mortgage the debt is unsecured: the lender can sue on the note but cannot foreclose.
The borrower gives the mortgage and is the **mortgagor**. The lender receives it and is the **mortgagee**.
**Hypothecation** is pledging property as collateral while keeping possession.
New York is a **lien-theory** state. The mortgagor keeps title and possession; the lender holds only a lien until a foreclosure sale.
A **deed of trust**, used in many other states, gives bare title to a trustee. It is not New York's standard instrument.
The mortgagor must pay the debt, pay taxes and assessments, keep the property insured, and keep it in repair. Breaking any of these duties is a **default**, not just missing payments.
Lenders usually collect taxes and insurance monthly in an **escrow account**, making the payment **PITI**.
Mortgage interest is paid **in arrears**: the payment due on the 1st covers the prior month's interest.
**Usury** is charging more than the legal maximum rate. In New York, 16% is the civil ceiling and over 25% is criminal usury.
Federal law exempts most first-lien home loans made by institutional lenders from usury limits.

sections.heading: Mortgage clauses
sections.intro: Questions usually describe what a clause does and ask for its name.
points: Without an **acceleration clause**, the lender could sue only for installments already past due, one at a time.
The federal **Garn–St Germain Act** bars enforcing a due-on-sale clause on a home with fewer than five units for listed transfers.
Protected transfers include the borrower's death, a transfer to a spouse or children, to a spouse under a divorce decree, or into the borrower's living trust.
**Prepayment penalties** on a New York owner-occupied 1–6 family or co-op loan above 6% interest are allowed only in the **first year**, and only if the note says so (GOL §5-501).
FHA, VA, and NY high-cost and subprime loans allow no prepayment penalty. Commercial loans often have them.
Late charges on owner-occupied 1–6 family and co-op loans start only after a payment is more than **15 days** late (the grace period). They never exceed **2%** of the installment (RPL §254-b).
FHA and VA loans are exempt from this late-charge cap.

sections.heading: Recording, lien priority, and payoff
sections.intro: Priority decides who is paid first from a foreclosure sale, and recording is what fixes priority.
points: Recording gives **constructive notice**. Record with the county clerk or, in most of NYC, the City Register.
Under New York's **race-notice** act, a later good-faith lender without notice who records first outranks an earlier unrecorded mortgage (RPL §291).
Liens generally rank in recording order. The **first mortgage** is senior; second mortgages and equity lines are **junior**.
Junior liens cost more because they are paid after senior liens.
**Real property tax liens** outrank mortgages regardless of date.
A foreclosure wipes out junior liens whose holders were **joined as defendants**; they claim against any surplus.
A foreclosure never wipes out a **senior** lien, so a buyer at a second-mortgage foreclosure takes subject to the first.
A lender can sell the loan by **assignment** without changing the borrower's obligations.
At payoff the lender must present a **satisfaction** for recording within **30 days** (RPL §275).
If the satisfaction is not presented within 30, 60, or 90 days, the lender owes the borrower $500, $1,000, or $1,500 (RPL §275, RPAPL §1921).
New York's **mortgage recording tax** is based on the loan amount.
A refinance done as a **CEMA** (consolidation, extension and modification agreement) is taxed only on new money.
A co-op share loan is secured by shares, not a recorded mortgage, so it pays no mortgage tax.

example.title: Worked example: distributing foreclosure proceeds
steps: A referee's sale brings $500,000. Costs and referee fees are $15,000; the first mortgage is owed $310,000; a joined second mortgage $120,000; a judgment docketed after both $20,000.
Step 1: Costs come off first: $500,000 − $15,000 = $485,000.
Step 2: Pay the first mortgage: $485,000 − $310,000 = $175,000.
Step 3: Pay the second mortgage: $175,000 − $120,000 = $55,000.
Step 4: Pay the judgment: $55,000 − $20,000 = $35,000.
Answer: the former owner receives the $35,000 surplus, last in line after every junior lien.

sections.heading: Selling a property that has a mortgage
sections.intro: There are three ways to sell mortgaged property. The key question is who is personally liable if the loan later defaults.
points: **Free and clear**: the seller's loan is paid off from the proceeds at closing and a satisfaction is recorded. This is the usual sale.
**Subject to the mortgage**: the buyer takes title and makes the payments but never promises to pay.
A subject-to buyer can lose the property, but only the seller, who signed the note, owes a deficiency.
**Assumption**: the buyer agrees to pay and becomes **primarily liable**.
After an assumption the seller stays **secondarily liable**, unless the lender grants a release or a **novation** (substituting the buyer as borrower).
Lenders often charge an assumption fee on the balance.
Subject-to sales and assumptions can both trigger the **due-on-sale clause**.
FHA and VA loans can be assumed by a creditworthy buyer with approval; most conventional loans cannot.

head: Method
Old loan
Buyer liable?
Seller liable?
rows: No; only the property is at risk

sections.heading: New York judicial foreclosure, step by step
sections.intro: New York lenders must sue to foreclose a mortgage. A default never lets them change the locks or sell without a court judgment.
points: Step 1, **default**: the servicer reviews workout options. Federal servicing rules generally bar a foreclosure filing until the loan is more than **120 days** delinquent.
Step 2, the **90-day notice**: mailed at least 90 days before suit on a home loan, listing at least five housing counseling agencies serving the county (RPAPL §1304).
The notice is reported to the Department of Financial Services (DFS) within 3 business days (RPAPL §1306).
A defective notice is a missing **condition precedent**, and the case can be dismissed.
Step 3, the **lawsuit**: a summons and complaint served with the 'Help for Homeowners in Foreclosure' notice (RPAPL §1303).
The lender also files a **notice of pendency (lis pendens)** with the county clerk. It gives constructive notice to later buyers and lenders and lasts **3 years** unless extended.
Step 4, the **settlement conference**: for owner-occupied home loans, held within **60 days** after proof of service is filed (CPLR 3408).
At the conference both sides must negotiate in **good faith**, but the court imposes no deal.
Step 5, **judgment of foreclosure and sale**, after a court-appointed referee computes the amount due.
Step 6, the **sale**: after published notice, a court-appointed **referee** auctions the property and delivers a referee's deed, with no warranties.
Sale proceeds pay costs, then liens in priority order, then the owner.
Step 7, **after the sale**: the lender may seek a deficiency. Residential tenants get notice and generally may stay at least 90 days or through their lease (RPAPL §1305).
Until the sale the borrower keeps the **equity of redemption**: paying the full debt, interest, and costs saves the home. There is **no statutory redemption** afterward.
The lender or servicer must maintain vacant, abandoned homes in default under the 2016 **zombie property law** (RPAPL §1308).
**Co-op exception**: a co-op loan is secured by shares and the proprietary lease, not a mortgage.
After a 90-day notice, the co-op lender sells the shares in a **nonjudicial** Uniform Commercial Code (UCC) sale, with no foreclosure lawsuit or referee (UCC §9-611(f)).

sections.heading: Deficiency judgments and alternatives to foreclosure
sections.intro: When the sale does not cover the debt, New York limits what the lender can collect personally. Several workouts can avoid foreclosure altogether.
points: A **deficiency judgment** is a personal judgment for the shortfall against anyone liable on the debt: the borrower, an assuming buyer, or a guarantor.
New York credits the borrower with the **higher** of the sale price or the court-determined **fair market value** (RPAPL §1371).
That rule stops a lender from buying cheaply at the auction and suing for an inflated balance.
The motion is due within **90 days** after the referee's deed is delivered. If the lender misses it, the sale proceeds count as **full satisfaction**.
Do not promise a seller that a short sale forgives the shortfall. That depends on the lender's written terms, so refer the seller to a lawyer.
Rescue firms may not collect fees until the owner signs an agreement with the lender (federal Regulation O).
New York distressed property consultants may not take fees before fully performing (RPL §265-b).

example.title: Worked example: maximum New York deficiency
steps: The judgment, with interest and costs, is $412,000. The auction brings $318,000, and the court finds the fair market value is $350,000.
Step 1: Credit the higher figure: $350,000.
Answer: at most $62,000, not $94,000, and only if the lender moves within 90 days of delivery of the referee's deed.

sections.heading: Mortgage market players
sections.intro: The primary market makes loans; the secondary market buys them so lenders can lend again.
points: **Primary market** lenders deal directly with borrowers: commercial banks, savings banks and savings and loan associations (thrifts), credit unions, mortgage bankers, and private lenders.
The **secondary market** buys loans and pools them into **mortgage-backed securities (MBS)**, replenishing lenders' funds.
**Conforming** loans meet Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac rules, including the loan limit. A **jumbo** (nonconforming) loan exceeds the limit; that does not make it illegal or subprime.
Fannie Mae (FNMA) and Freddie Mac (FHLMC) are congressionally chartered **government-sponsored enterprises (GSEs)**. They have been in Federal Housing Finance Agency conservatorship since 2008.
**Ginnie Mae** (GNMA) is a government-owned corporation within the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD).
New York's Department of Financial Services (DFS) registers **mortgage brokers** and licenses **mortgage bankers** (Banking Law Article 12-D).
Individual mortgage loan originators need their own license through the Nationwide Multistate Licensing System, NMLS (Banking Law Article 12-E).
A real estate license alone does **not** authorize arranging residential mortgage loans.
A firm that is both the seller's real estate broker and the buyer's mortgage broker must disclose the dual role at its first substantive contact with the buyer.
The buyer and seller must sign the **mortgage broker dual agency disclosure** before mortgage services begin (3 NYCRR §38.12).
Mortgage brokers also use a **pre-application disclosure and fee agreement**.
A **lender rebate** toward closing costs usually comes with a higher rate.

Role
Exam angle
rows: Funds and closes loans in its own name, often sells them
Arranges loans with lenders for a fee
Does not fund loans or issue commitments
GSEs that buy conforming loans and issue MBS

Collects payments, runs escrow, handles defaults

sections.heading: Loan types and mortgage insurance
sections.intro: Loans are first sorted by who backs them. Government backing and mortgage insurance protect the lender, not the borrower.
points: A **conventional** loan has no government insurance or guarantee.
The **loan-to-value (LTV)** ratio is loan ÷ value. Above 80% LTV, the lender usually requires **private mortgage insurance (PMI)**, which the borrower pays to protect the lender.
Under the federal **Homeowners Protection Act (HPA)**, a current borrower with a good payment history may request PMI cancellation in writing at **80%** of original value.
PMI ends automatically when the balance is scheduled to reach **78%**, and no later than the loan's **midpoint**.
**Original value** is the lower of price or appraisal; on a refinance, it is the appraisal.
A rise in market value does not trigger HPA cancellation. A lender or investor may still allow removal based on a new appraisal.
**FHA** insures loans made by approved lenders. The minimum down payment is **3.5%** with a 580+ score, or 10% at 500–579.
FHA charges an up-front mortgage insurance premium (MIP), usually financed. The annual MIP lasts for the **life of the loan** if under 10% down, or 11 years with 10% or more.
The HPA cancellation rules do not apply to MIP.
The **VA** guarantees part of loans to eligible veterans, service members, and some surviving spouses, shown by a **Certificate of Eligibility**.
With full entitlement and a price no higher than the appraisal, a VA loan needs **no down payment** and no monthly mortgage insurance, only a one-time **funding fee**.
The VA funding fee is waived for those receiving service-connected disability compensation. The home must be owner-occupied.
FHA and VA contracts include an **amendatory (escape) clause**: the buyer may cancel without losing the deposit if the appraisal is below the price. Neither allows prepayment penalties.
USDA's **Rural Housing Service** makes or guarantees loans in eligible rural areas, often with no down payment.
The **State of New York Mortgage Agency (SONYMA)**, part of NYS Homes and Community Renewal, sells tax-exempt bonds to fund below-market loans and down payment help through participating lenders.
SONYMA generally serves **first-time buyers**: no primary home owned in the past 3 years. Exceptions apply in target areas and for qualified veterans. Income and price limits apply.

head: Loan
Backing

Mortgage insurance
rows: PMI if LTV is over 80%; cancellable

example.title: Worked example: when PMI can come off
steps: A buyer pays $500,000 for a home that appraises at $520,000 and takes a conventional loan with PMI.
Step 1: Original value = the lower of price or appraisal = $500,000.
Step 2: Request point = $500,000 × 80% = a $400,000 balance.
Step 3: Automatic point = $500,000 × 78% = a $390,000 balance, or the loan's midpoint if that comes first.
Answer: $400,000 and $390,000. Using the $520,000 appraisal is the trap.

sections.heading: Repayment plans and special-purpose loans
sections.intro: Most questions describe a loan structure and ask for its name, so learn the one feature that defines each.
points: A **fully amortizing fixed-rate** loan has a level principal-and-interest (P&I) payment that retires the debt by maturity. Early payments are mostly interest.
A **straight (term) loan** is interest-only, with all principal due at the end.
A **balloon** loan does not fully amortize, leaving a large final payment.
A **graduated payment mortgage** starts with low payments that rise on schedule and may negatively amortize early.
A **pledged-account** mortgage draws on a pledged deposit to supplement the early payments.
A **buydown** lowers the rate with points (permanent) or with an up-front subsidy for the first years (temporary, such as 2-1).
A **construction loan** pays out in draws, charging interest only on money advanced. A permanent **takeout loan** pays it off.
A **reverse mortgage** pays the owner from equity with no monthly loan payment. FHA's version is the Home Equity Conversion Mortgage (HECM), for owners aged **62+**.
A reverse-mortgage owner keeps title but must pay taxes, insurance, and upkeep. The loan comes due when the last borrower dies, sells, or moves out.

example.title: Worked example: splitting the first two payments
steps: A $320,000 loan for 30 years at 6% has a P&I payment of $1,918.56.
Step 6: Total interest over 30 years is about $1,918.56 × 360 − $320,000 = $370,682.
Answer: interest falls and principal rises every month; total interest is about $370,682.

sections.heading: Adjustable-rate mortgages
sections.intro: Lenders build expected **inflation** into rates. On a fixed-rate loan the lender bears the risk that rates rise; an adjustable-rate mortgage (ARM) shifts that risk to the borrower. Every ARM question uses the index, margin, caps, and adjustment schedule.
points: The **index** is a published market rate the lender does not control, such as a Treasury yield or the Secured Overnight Financing Rate (SOFR). SOFR replaced the London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR).
The **margin** is the lender's fixed markup and never changes.
**Fully indexed rate = index + margin.** A discounted teaser rate is not part of the formula; it simply expires.
Caps come in three kinds: an initial-adjustment cap, a **periodic cap** on each later change, and a **lifetime cap (ceiling)** over the initial rate. They are often written 2/2/5.
A **payment cap** limits dollars, not the rate. Unpaid interest can then be added to the balance: **negative amortization**.
A **5/1 ARM** is fixed for 5 years, then adjusts yearly. A 5/6 ARM adjusts every 6 months after year 5.
Lenders give the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) ARM booklet (CHARM) and program disclosures at application.

example.title: Worked example: applying the caps
steps: An ARM starts at 4.75% with a 2.75% margin, a 2% periodic cap, and a 5% lifetime cap (ceiling 9.75%).
Adjustment 1: 4.20% index + 2.75% = 6.95%.
The periodic cap allows only 6.75%, so the new rate is 6.75%.
The cap allows up to 8.75%, so the new rate is 7.85%.
The periodic cap allows 9.85%, but the ceiling is 9.75%, so the new rate is 9.75%.
Answer: compute index + margin first; the lowest applicable cap wins. Never add the margin to the old rate or the teaser rate.

sections.heading: Points and APR
sections.intro: Points and the annual percentage rate (APR) measure the cost of credit beyond the note rate.
points: One **point** equals **1% of the loan amount**.
**Discount points** are prepaid interest that buy down the rate. **Origination** points pay the lender for making the loan.
Paying points makes sense only if the borrower keeps the loan past the break-even month.
The **APR** is the yearly cost of credit: the note rate plus prepaid **finance charges** such as points, origination and broker fees, and mortgage insurance.
A loan with points therefore has an APR above its note rate.
For real estate loans, reasonable appraisal, title, credit report, and recording fees are **not** finance charges.
Taxes, escrow deposits, and the down payment never enter the APR.
An APR increase of more than 1/8 of a percentage point after the Closing Disclosure (most loans) restarts the 3-business-day wait.
Mortgage interest and purchase points may be tax-deductible (see the income tax chapter).

example.title: Worked example: points and APR on one loan
steps: A buyer borrows $300,000 toward a $375,000 price at 6.00% for 30 years, paying 2 discount points, a $1,500 origination fee, a $650 appraisal, and $1,800 in title charges.
Step 1: Points = $300,000 × 2% = $6,000. Using 2% of the price, $7,500, is the trap.
Step 2: Prepaid finance charges = $6,000 + $1,500 = $7,500. The appraisal and title charges are excluded.
Step 3: The P&I payment is $1,798.65.
Step 5: The rate at which $1,798.65 a month for 360 months repays $292,500 is about 6.24%.
Answer: note rate 6.00%, APR about 6.24%.

sections.heading: TILA, RESPA, ECOA, and other lending laws
sections.intro: Each federal law has one job; questions describe a problem and ask which law applies.
points: The **Truth in Lending Act (TILA)** requires disclosure of the finance charge and APR, regulates credit ads, and grants rescission. It does not set rates.
TILA is Title I of the Consumer Credit Protection Act and is carried out by **Regulation Z**.
**Rescission** applies to a refinance or home equity loan or line secured by the **principal residence**.
The borrower may cancel until midnight of the **third business day** after signing and receiving the disclosures and notice. Saturdays count; Sundays and federal holidays do not.
A **purchase** mortgage has no rescission right. A refinance with the same lender can be rescinded only as to new money.
Missing disclosures can extend the rescission right up to 3 years.
A **triggering term** in an ad (down payment, number of payments or repayment period, payment amount, or finance charge) requires the down payment, the repayment terms, and the **APR**.
The APR alone or 'easy terms' triggers nothing. Licensees who advertise financing must comply.
**TRID** (the TILA-RESPA Integrated Disclosure rule): the **Loan Estimate** is due within 3 business days after application.
Application here means the borrower's name, income, Social Security number, property address, estimated value, and loan amount.
The borrower must receive the **Closing Disclosure** at least **3 business days before consummation**.
The **Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act (RESPA)**, carried out by Regulation X, covers federally related 1–4 family loans.
RESPA bans **kickbacks** and unearned fees. Pay for real services and cooperating-broker splits are allowed (RESPA Section 8).
A seller may not require a particular title insurer (RESPA Section 9).
The escrow cushion is capped at **one-sixth** (about 2 months) of a year's escrow disbursements (RESPA Section 10).

The **Equal Credit Opportunity Act (ECOA)**, Regulation B, bars credit discrimination by race, color, religion, national origin, sex, **marital status**, age (if able to contract), public-assistance income, or exercising credit rights.
Marital status, age, and public assistance are not federal Fair Housing Act classes.
Under ECOA, notice of action is due within **30 days** of a completed application.
The **Fair Housing Act** and New York's Human Rights Law bar lending discrimination, including **redlining**: refusing or worsening loans in an area because of its racial or ethnic makeup.
Home Mortgage Disclosure Act (HMDA) data exposes redlining. The **Community Reinvestment Act** (1977) rates banks on serving their whole community.

head: Law
Purpose
Key numbers
rows: 3 business days to rescind non-purchase loans on a principal home
Escrow cushion up to 1/6 of a year's escrow disbursements
Weighed on bank branch and merger applications

example.title: Worked example: counting the rescission period
steps: A homeowner closes a refinance of her principal home with a new lender on a Friday and receives all disclosures and notices that day. Monday is a federal holiday.
Step 1: Saturday is day 1, because Saturdays count for rescission.
Step 2: Skip Sunday and the Monday holiday; Tuesday is day 2 and Wednesday is day 3.
Answer: she may rescind until midnight Wednesday, and the lender cannot disburse the funds before then.

sections.heading: Underwriting and qualifying ratios
sections.intro: **Underwriting** is the lender's risk review of the property and the borrower. Ratios in exam problems are stated assumptions, not universal law.
points: **Property**: the lender bases the loan on the **lower** of the price or appraised value.
The lender also weighs location, condition, comparables, and type: 1–4 family, owner-occupied, or income-producing, which needs more down.
Example: price $500,000, appraisal $480,000, 90% LTV gives a $432,000 loan. The buyer needs $68,000 down, not $50,000.
**Borrower**: verified, stable income likely to continue, credit reports, liquid assets and reserves, and monthly debts.
Income usually needs a two-year history. A self-employed sole proprietor, partner, or corporate owner usually shows two years of tax returns.
Federal **ability-to-repay** rules require a good-faith finding that the borrower can repay.
**Front-end (housing) ratio** = PITI ÷ gross monthly income.
**Back-end (total debt) ratio** = (PITI + other monthly debts) ÷ gross monthly income.
Traditional guides: conventional **28/36**, FHA 31/43, and VA 41% total debt plus a residual-income test.
**Prequalification** is an informal estimate from unverified information.
**Preapproval** follows an application, credit check, and verification.
A **mortgage commitment** is the lender's written approval on stated terms, usually with conditions.
A **rate lock** holds a quoted rate for a set period.

example.title: Worked example: maximum PITI and loan amount
steps: A buyer earns $108,000 a year and pays $1,000 a month on other debts. The lender uses 28/36.
Step 1: Gross monthly income = $108,000 ÷ 12 = $9,000.
Step 2: Front-end limit = $9,000 × 28% = $2,520.
Step 3: Back-end total = $9,000 × 36% = $3,240.
Step 4: Back-end limit = $3,240 − $1,000 other debts = $2,240.
Step 5: Maximum PITI = the lower figure, $2,240.
Step 6: With $540 a month for taxes and insurance, P&I can be $1,700.
Answer: $2,240 PITI and about a $283,500 loan. Subtracting the debts from the front-end limit is the trap.

sections.heading: Predatory lending and mortgage fraud
sections.intro: Predatory lending is a set of abusive practices rather than one statute. Licensees should spot the red flags and refer clients to housing counselors or lawyers.
points: **Subprime** loans charge more because of weaker credit and are legal by themselves.
Lending becomes **predatory** through hidden fees, equity stripping, unaffordable balloon payments, or ignoring the ability to repay.
**Loan flipping** is repeated refinancing, often of elderly owners, that piles on points and fees without real benefit.
Illegal **property flipping** is different: a quick resale at a price propped up by an inflated appraisal.
Rolling credit card debt into a home equity loan turns unsecured debt into debt secured by the home.
**Mortgage fraud** includes inflated appraisals, **straw buyers**, falsified income, and undisclosed cash back to the buyer.

New York **high-cost home loans** may not include flipping without a tangible net benefit, financed **single-premium credit insurance**, negative amortization, or prepayment penalties (Banking Law §6-l).
High-cost lenders must also give a notice at application recommending financial counseling, with a Department of Financial Services (DFS) list of counselors (Banking Law §6-l).
**Subprime** home loans in New York carry ability-to-repay, escrow, and no-prepayment-penalty rules (Banking Law §6-m).
Federally, the Home Ownership and Equity Protection Act (HOEPA, 1994) restricts high-cost mortgages.

head: Practice
What it looks like
Main protection
rows: Frequent refinances with new fees and no benefit
Lending on equity, not the ability to repay
Single-premium credit insurance financed into the loan
Charges that appear or grow at closing
Targeting protected groups or areas for worse loans
Fair Housing Act, ECOA, NY Human Rights Law
Up-front fees or deed transfers to 'save' a home

guides.title: Land Use Regulations
guides.overview: How government and private parties limit land use: the four government powers (PETE), New York planning and zoning, variances, nonconforming uses, subdivisions, building codes, SEQR, wetlands, eminent domain and deed restrictions. The exam hits classification (police power or eminent domain? use or area variance?), New York procedure (who decides, which deadline, how many votes) and short calculations.

numbers.label: Appeal a zoning officer's ruling to the ZBA, counted from its filing
ZBA must decide within 62 days after the hearing
Article 78 against a ZBA decision, counted from filing with the town clerk
ZBA votes: 2 of 3, 3 of 5, 4 of 7, even with absences
Votes of all members needed to act against a county disapproval or modification
Protest by owners of 20% of the rezoned land or land within 100 feet
Town board vote needed to rezone after a valid protest
File the signed final plat with the county clerk or the approval expires
Lots of 5 acres or less: health department approves water and sewage before sale
Buyer's cancellation right under ILSFDA and NY RPL Article 9-A
ILSFDA revocation right if no property report was given
NYC began requiring certificates of occupancy
Flood chance in a Special Flood Hazard Area (100-year floodplain)
Regulated adjacent area around a DEC freshwater wetland
Maximum regulated adjacent area beside a tidal wetland
Challenge a condemnor's public-use findings in the Appellate Division
Euclid v. Ambler Realty upheld use-district zoning

mustKnow: **PETE**: police power, eminent domain, taxation, escheat. Only **eminent domain** pays the owner.
**Police power** (health, safety, morals, welfare) supports zoning, codes, subdivision rules and rent regulation. A valid rule owes **no compensation**, even if value drops.
**Eminent domain** requires public use and **just compensation**: fair market value at highest and best use. Condemnation is the process. No owner consent is needed.
**Escheat**: the State takes property of an owner who dies with no will and no heirs. **Tax foreclosure** is taxation, not eminent domain.
Only the elected **legislative body** adopts or amends zoning. The **ZBA cannot rezone**.
Zoning must follow the **comprehensive plan**, which the legislative body adopts. Until a rezoning, the **current zoning controls**.
**Planning board** (appointed): plats, site plans, cluster plans, often special permits. **ZBA** (quasi-judicial): appeals, interpretations, variances.

**Use variance** needs **unnecessary hardship**: no reasonable return from every permitted use, shown by competent financial evidence; a unique hardship; no change to neighborhood character; not self-created.
**Area variance** uses a **balancing test**: benefit vs detriment, five factors. Self-created difficulty counts but is not fatal.
Variances: the ZBA grants the **minimum** relief and may add land-related conditions. A variance **runs with the land**.
A **special use permit** approves a use the ordinance already allows once standards are met. **No hardship** showing is needed. The legislative body designates the issuing board.

A **lawful nonconforming use** **survives a sale**. It generally cannot expand, switch to another nonconforming use, or resume after the discontinuance period, whatever the intent. Amortization can end it.
**Spot zoning** (small parcel, owner's benefit, against the plan) is invalid. A small rezoning that **follows the plan** is valid.
A **protest** by owners of 20% of the land, or of land within 100 feet, means a rezoning needs **three-fourths** of the town board.
ZBA timeline: appeal within 60 days; decision within 62 days after the hearing. Any action needs a **majority of the full board**.
Challenge a ZBA decision by an **Article 78** proceeding in Supreme Court within **30 days** of its filing with the town clerk. A rational decision stands.
**Subdivision**: the planning board approves the plat. File the signed plat with the county clerk within **62 days**. A performance bond can secure unbuilt improvements.
**Cluster** = same density on smaller lots. **PUD** = mixed uses under one plan.
**Incentive zoning** = bonus for amenities. **TDR** = development rights moved to a receiving area.
A **building permit** authorizes construction. A **certificate of occupancy** authorizes occupancy for the stated use; a use change needs an amended CO.
Outside NYC, the **Uniform Code** sets minimums. Stricter local rules need Code Council approval, and code variances go to DOS **regional boards of review**.
NYC has its own codes, enforced by its Department of Buildings (DOB).
**SEQR** covers **discretionary** agency actions; ministerial acts are excluded.
SEQR types: **Type I** (Full EAF, EIS likelier), **Type II** (no review), Unlisted (everything else).
SEQR order: EAF → negative or positive declaration → draft EIS and comment → final EIS → findings.
DEC (freshwater and tidal), localities and the Army Corps (§404) may all regulate a wetland, including its **adjacent areas**. Get a current **jurisdictional determination**.
The **Adirondack Park Agency (APA)** controls private land in the Park: Hamlet is densest, Resource Management strictest. Forest Preserve land is **forever wild**.
**Inverse condemnation** = owner sues over a de facto taking. A partial taking adds **severance damages**.
**Covenants** bind later owners through recording. The **stricter** of zoning or covenant controls, and a variance doesn't release a covenant.
A deed **condition** with a right of re-entry can forfeit title. Covenant breach brings an injunction or damages.
**Laches** can bar slow enforcers. **Discriminatory covenants** are unenforceable (Shelley v. Kraemer).
The federal **ILSFDA** requires a **property report** before signing. The buyer can revoke within 7 days, or 2 years if no report was given.
**RPL Article 9-A**: installment sales of vacant subdivided land to NY residents need a DOS filing. Buyers may cancel within 7 days.

traps.trap: A zoning change that lowers my land's value entitles me to compensation.
traps.truth: Zoning is police power. Compensation is owed only for eminent domain or a regulation so severe it becomes a taking.

traps.trap: The ZBA can rezone a street to match the comprehensive plan.
traps.truth: Rezoning is legislative (town board, village board, city council). The plan guides; the current zoning controls until amended.

traps.trap: A self-created problem kills any variance.
traps.truth: It bars a use variance, but for an area variance it is only one factor in the balancing test.

traps.trap: Showing a store would earn more, or that the current use loses money, proves hardship.
traps.truth: The owner must show, with competent financial evidence, no reasonable return from every permitted use.

traps.trap: A special use permit is a variance granted by the ZBA after proof of hardship.
traps.truth: It approves a use the ordinance already allows if standards are met. No hardship; the issuing board is often the planning board.

traps.trap: A nonconforming use ends when the property is sold.
traps.truth: It runs with the land. It ends through discontinuance, amortization or destruction rules, and generally cannot expand or switch to another nonconforming use. Older textbooks (including Spada) say a sale ends it.

traps.trap: The owner always meant to reopen, so the discontinued nonconforming use survives.
traps.truth: Once the ordinance's discontinuance period runs, the right is lost regardless of intent (Toys "R" Us v. Silva).

traps.trap: You have 4 months to sue over a ZBA decision.
traps.truth: 30 days from filing with the town clerk. Four months is the general Article 78 limit; 60 days is the appeal to the ZBA.

traps.trap: A 3–2 vote of the five members present passes on a seven-member ZBA.
traps.truth: A majority of the full board is required: 4 of 7.

traps.trap: A building permit lets the buyer move in once the house is framed.
traps.truth: Occupancy requires a certificate of occupancy (or temporary CO) after inspection.

traps.trap: Every project needs an EIS, and Type I means an automatic EIS.
traps.truth: Only a positive declaration requires an EIS; Type II needs no review and ministerial permits are outside SEQR.

traps.trap: Building on dry ground near a marsh avoids any wetland permit.
traps.truth: Adjacent areas are regulated: 100 feet for freshwater, up to 300 feet (150 in NYC) for tidal wetlands.

traps.trap: A 100-year floodplain floods once a century.
traps.truth: It has a 1% chance every year, about 26% over a 30-year mortgage.

traps.trap: A ZBA variance overrides a stricter recorded covenant.
traps.truth: Both apply and the stricter controls; covenant holders can still sue.

mnemonics.name: PETE
mnemonics.meaning: Police power, Eminent domain, Taxation, Escheat: the four government powers over private land. Only eminent domain pays the owner.

mnemonics.name: U goes with U
mnemonics.meaning: Use variance needs Unnecessary hardship; the area variance gets the balancing test.

formulas.name: Density with a bonus
formulas.formula: Units = acres × units per acre × (1 + bonus %)

formulas.name: Inclusionary split

formulas.name: Variance substantiality
